entries.originalText: Cease to complain; consider My suffering and that of My saints.
entries.modernizedText: Cease to complain; consider My suffering and that of My saints.

entries.originalText: Thou hast not yet resisted unto blood.(1) It is little which thou sufferest in comparison with those who have suffered so many things, have been so strongly tempted, so grievously troubled, so manywise proved and tried.
entries.modernizedText: You have not yet resisted to the point of blood.(1) It is little that you suffer in comparison with those who have suffered so many things, have been so strongly tempted, so grievously troubled, tested and tried in so many ways.

entries.originalText: Thou oughtest therefore to call to mind the more grievous sufferings of others that thou mightest bear thy lesser ones more easily, and if they seem not to thee little, see that it is not thy impatience which is the cause of this.
entries.modernizedText: You ought therefore to call to mind the more grievous sufferings of others, that you might bear your lesser ones more easily; and if they do not seem little to you, see that your impatience is not the cause of this.

entries.originalText: But whether they be little or whether they be great, study to bear them all with patience.
entries.modernizedText: But whether they are little or great, study to bear them all with patience.

entries.originalText: “So far as thou settest thyself to bear patiently, so far thou dost wisely and art deserving of the more merit; thou shalt also bear the more easily if thy mind and habit are carefully trained hereunto.
entries.modernizedText: “As far as you set yourself to bear patiently, so far you act wisely and deserve the more merit; you will also bear more easily if your mind and habit are carefully trained for this.

entries.originalText: And say not ‘I cannot bear these things from such a man, nor are things of this kind to be borne by me, for he hath done me grievous harm and imputeth to me what I had never thought: but from another I will suffer patiently, such things as I see I ought to suffer.’
entries.modernizedText: And do not say, ‘I cannot bear these things from such a man, nor are things of this kind to be borne by me, for he has done me grievous harm and imputes to me what I had never thought; but from another I will suffer patiently such things as I see I ought to suffer.’

entries.originalText: Foolish is such a thought as this, for it considereth not the virtue of patience, nor by whom that virtue is to be crowned, but it rather weigheth persons and offences against self.
entries.modernizedText: Foolish is such a thought as this, for it does not consider the virtue of patience, nor by whom that virtue is to be crowned, but rather weighs persons and offenses against self.

entries.originalText: “He is not truly patient who will only suffer as far as seemeth right to himself and from whom he pleaseth.
entries.modernizedText: “He is not truly patient who will only suffer as far as seems right to himself and from whom he pleases.

entries.originalText: But the truly patient man considereth not by what man he is tried, whether by one above him, or by an equal or inferior, whether by a good and holy man, or a perverse and unworthy; but indifferently from every creature, whatsoever or how often soever adversity happeneth to him, he gratefully accepteth all from the hand of God and counteth it great gain: for with God nothing which is borne for His sake, however small, shall lose its reward.
entries.modernizedText: But the truly patient man does not consider by what man he is tried, whether by one above him, or by an equal or inferior, whether by a good and holy man, or a perverse and unworthy one; but without distinction, from every creature, whatever adversity happens to him or however often, he gratefully accepts all from the hand of God and counts it great gain: for with God nothing that is borne for His sake, however small, will lose its reward.

entries.originalText: “Be thou therefore ready for the fight if thou wilt have the victory.
entries.modernizedText: “Be therefore ready for the fight if you would have the victory.

entries.originalText: Without striving thou canst not win the crown of patience; if thou wilt not suffer thou refusest to be crowned.
entries.modernizedText: Without striving you cannot win the crown of patience; if you will not suffer you refuse to be crowned.

entries.originalText: But if thou desirest to be crowned, strive manfully, endure patiently.
entries.modernizedText: But if you desire to be crowned, strive manfully, endure patiently.

entries.originalText: Without labour thou drawest not near to rest, nor without fighting comest thou to victory.”
entries.modernizedText: Without labor you do not draw near to rest, nor without fighting do you come to victory.”

entries.originalText: Make possible to me, O Lord, by grace what seemeth impossible to me by nature.
entries.modernizedText: Make possible to me, O Lord, by grace what seems impossible to me by nature.

entries.originalText: Thou knowest how little I am able to bear, and how quickly I am cast down when a like adversity riseth up against me.
entries.modernizedText: You know how little I am able to bear, and how quickly I am cast down when a similar adversity rises up against me.

entries.originalText: Whatsoever trial of tribulation may come to me, may it become unto me pleasing and acceptable, for to suffer and be vexed for Thy sake is exceeding healthful to the soul.
entries.modernizedText: Whatever trial of tribulation may come to me, may it become pleasing and acceptable to me, for to suffer and be vexed for Your sake is exceedingly beneficial to the soul.
